rationale: The NIST/Virginia Tech paper presents combinatorial testing as a quantitative measure of selected dataset usefulness and expressly says the relation of this input coverage to model performance is not yet clear. Its transfer-learning discussion identifies cases where even large data volumes are insufficient. Those qualifications support, rather than undermine, the claim that selected coverage cannot alone establish performance or safe-operation probability.
evidence_locators: S-EVID-002-R1, 'Assured Autonomy through Combinatorial Methods', PDF p. 3
S-EVID-002-R2, 'Assured Autonomy through Combinatorial Methods', PDF p. 5
limitations: No case-specific choice of ODD factors, discretization, interaction strength, or unmodeled-factor test was available for review.
The paper is a method proposal, not a validated certification or system safety result.
